processes.name: Sitara deal extension / roll requests to clear allocation exceptions
processes.description: Volume management and logistics staff find meters with flow but an expired or missing Sitara deal and email Daren Farmer (or Stacey) to extend or roll the ticket so the allocation exception clears. The trader checks the contract, edits the deal, and replies by email, often after several back-and-forths.
processes.stall_points: Each request waits on one person (Daren) to check contracts and edit the ticket; the requester cannot close the exception or set up the accounting arrangement until the answer arrives, and contract questions are passed on again to Julie Meyers.
processes.automation: Flag deals that expire while a meter still flows (or lack an evergreen flag) and propose the extension to the deal owner for one-click approval, instead of each analyst emailing the same request.

processes.name: Month-end intercompany and pipeline volume variance clearing
processes.description: Settlements and volume management staff list Sitara deals with volume variances or a missing purchase or sale side, then chase schedulers to fix pathing, desk-to-desk deals and swing contracts before the close. Answers come by email and often require a meeting or repeated follow-up.
processes.stall_points: Same variances are re-raised across weeks because the person who must re-path or create the deal is busy; the analyst has to forward the original email with a nudge and sometimes ask for a meeting to explain.
processes.automation: Run a monthly accrual-vs-nomination comparison that lists one-sided or mismatched intercompany deals and routes each to the owning scheduler with a due date.

processes.name: Counterparty invoice and price discrepancy resolution
processes.description: Settlements and accounting staff find that a counterparty's invoice or price does not match Sitara or Unify, and email Daren Farmer or Julie Meyers to confirm the correct deal, trader or price. Fixes are then keyed into Sitara or done via accounting arrangements.
processes.stall_points: Requests sit with Daren or Julie, who forward to others (Craig, traders at the counterparty); invoice due dates pass and settlements has to chase again.
processes.automation: Auto-compare invoice lines against Sitara deal price, entity and volume and send the exception with the supporting deal data to one queue, so settlements does not hunt for the trader or confirmation.

processes.name: Producer and customer nomination changes relayed and re-keyed
processes.description: Producers and customers (KCS Josey Ranch, Reliant, wellhead producers, methanol and MTBE plants, power plants) send revised nominations by email or spreadsheet. A trade-support person forwards each revision to Daren, Tom Acton and others, who then re-key the volumes in Sitara or spreadsheets.
processes.stall_points: Revisions arrive several times a month (1st, 2nd, 3rd rev for Josey) and each is forwarded manually; recipients can be missed from the send list, and some requests sit until someone replies.
processes.automation: Parse incoming nomination emails and attachments into a structured nomination change, diff against the current Sitara volume and prepare the update for approval.

processes.name: Unaccounted-for (UA4) and zero-volume feed monitoring and correction
processes.description: Analysts watch daily P&L and imbalance numbers for UA4 swings, find meters where MIPS/POPS fed zero volumes to Sitara or MOPS, and manually override them with estimates. A team was assembled to reconcile 1999 UA4, with email escalation to measurement.
processes.stall_points: The root fix sits with another system team that treated it as not a priority, so analysts override zeros by hand each night and re-check the next day to see if it held.
processes.automation: Alert automatically when a meter feed drops to zero while nominations are positive, and show UA4 movement by meter in the nightly P&L so overrides are targeted.

processes.name: Daily P&L calculation and distribution
processes.description: After entering deals and running the calc, a book owner emails the daily P&L (with notes on deal changes, held-back amounts and UA4 positions) to traders and desk heads. Questions about the numbers are answered by follow-up email.
processes.stall_points: The calc depends on the system being up (deals missed the run when it went down) and unexplained P&L adjustments need a call or email to reconcile.
processes.automation: Generate and send the daily P&L summary and UA4 balance per book automatically after the calc completes, flagging unexplained adjustments.

processes.name: Transport rate verification and PMA clearing
processes.description: Transport and settlement analysts check pipeline rates and contract allocations against Unify and Sitara usage tickets and clear price mismatch adjustments (PMAs). Discrepancies are emailed to schedulers who must confirm numbers with the pipeline.
processes.stall_points: Rates live in two systems (Unify for invoicing, Sitara tickets for P&L) so they are corrected twice; the scheduler cannot give a time frame and the issue stays open across weeks.
processes.automation: Compare contract rates in the rate matrix, Unify and Sitara usage tickets automatically each month and list mismatches for one person to correct.

processes.name: Cost allocation surveys, labor reports and department admin requests
processes.description: Finance and admin groups send recurring monthly surveys (hours, activity drivers), labor distribution checks, O&M reports and vacation or hiring requests that managers fill in and return by a deadline. Each is a spreadsheet or email that must be filled in by hand each month.
processes.stall_points: Surveys come with tight deadlines and manual spreadsheet entry; reports go to the wrong person (Daren was not receiving the Labor Distribution report) and must be chased.
processes.automation: Pre-fill the survey from last month and existing reports, and route labor and O&M reports to the right managers automatically.

processes.name: Customer plant and pipeline outage notices relayed to schedulers
processes.description: Plant upset updates (methanol, MTBE), customer outages and pipeline maintenance are emailed to a distribution list or forwarded by hand to schedulers. Schedulers then decide whether to zero volumes, arrange buybacks or find alternate supply.
processes.stall_points: Updates arrive as repeated emails that revise earlier forecasts, and the nomination decision (zero volumes, buyback) waits for a trader to reply.
processes.automation: Tag outage notices to affected meters and nominations and prompt the scheduler with a proposed volume change and status history.
